id: dec-0060
kind: decision
title: Track run state with a checkpoint file, not a daemon
state: accepted

edges:
  - type: derives_from
    to: int-0002
    note: cold-start latency is the UX; a daemon pays it once at boot and again at every crash recovery
alternatives:
  - option: a daemon
    why_not: >
      violates the single-binary intent (int-0002)
    revisit_if: cold-start latency stops being the binding constraint
  - option: a systemd or launchd unit that keeps dira running in the background
    why_not: >
      still a long-lived process the user must install and keep alive, which
      is the exact ceremony int-0002 rejects even though it never touches the
      network
  - option: a separate watcher binary that polls for crashed runs
    why_not: >
      adds a second binary to distribute and version alongside dira,
      doubling the release surface for a job a single checkpoint write
      already does
  - option: no persistence — a crashed run restarts from scratch
    why_not: >
      throws away the completed portion of a long run and reintroduces the
      exact latency and wasted work the checkpoint file exists to avoid

Fixture entry for `internal/enforcer`. This is the entry the canonical `dira
check` demo (`README.md`; `.agents/product-marketing.md` §6) is built on: the
plan `"add a background daemon to track run state"` must conflict with the `a
daemon` alternative above and cite exactly that `why_not` and `revisit_if`.

On resume, dira reads the last-written checkpoint at startup and continues
from there — no replay, no daemon, no separate process. See `dec-0042` for a
related but distinct question (event sourcing, rejected on different
grounds) and `cst-0004` for the standing constraint this decision also
satisfies.
